newsitem.title: USA: Hilton executives resign after Missouri inquiry.
newsitem.headline: Hilton executives resign after Missouri inquiry.

text.p: Three top executives of Hilton Hotels Corp., including its former president, have resigned in the wake of an investigation into a $250,000 grant made by Hilton to a local Missouri organization.

The resignations, announced on Friday at a Missouri Gaming Commission hearing, affected Raymond Avansino, former president and a current Hilton board member, Michael O'Brien, executive vice president of gaming development and Mark Rousseau, senior vice president of gaming development.

The inquiry, being conducted by the Missouri regulatory board, stems from the grant made to an associate of the former head of Kansas City's port authority, Elbert Anderson. He was involved in initial talks over Hilton's operation of a riverboat near the city, according to a story in the Los Angeles Times on Saturday.
A Hilton spokesman confirmed the resignations, but he declined to discuss the gaming commission's inquiry.
"We're taking a very forward-looking approach and look forward to getting open soon," Marc Grossman, senior vice president for corporate affairs, said in an interview.

Hilton is spending about $110 million on its Kansas City Flamingo hotel and riverboat casino complex near Kansas City. When opened, the riverboat will have more than 1,000 slot machines and 60 table games. A Hilton Garden Inn is scheduled to be open at the site in mid-1997.

But the riverboat's launch, which Hilton had planned for this summer, is being delayed while the commission looks into the grant, which was made to a local organization called K.C. Perspectives. The group runs business seminars for minority women and under Hilton's final agreement to develop the casino, it had pledged to make grants to local non-profit organizations.

Following Friday's hearing, the Missouri commission gave a preliminary approval of the riverboat's "suitability." Hilton now must complete an initial test cruise, after which the commission votes on a formal approval, Grossman said.
He said no set timetable existed for the commission's final vote. The test cruise is set for Thursday, October 17.

The inquiry comes at a crucial time for Hilton as it seeks to win final approvals from other state agencies to complete its three billion dollar acquisition of Bally Entertainment Corp. That deal would make it the largest hotel and gambling company in the United States.
